AirPlay engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume AirPlay capability in the binary covers storefront language. AVFoundation, MediaPlayer, and Connect actually separate casting behavior from product-page copy:

  • AVRoutePickerView & MPVolumeView — surface AirPlay destination pickers and volume routing in your app. Control which receivers appear. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • AVPlayer external playback & route sharing — hands video or audio streams to Apple TV, HomePod, or compatible receivers. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains cast-to-TV value to buyers.
  • In-app casting UI — device lists, now-playing on TV chrome, speaker group labels, and connection status text. Your listing may mention AirPlay; implementing route pickers is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of AirPlay support in the binary.

Working AirPlay in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

What China buyers still see when the zh-Hans row is incomplete

When Simplified Chinese metadata is missing or falls back to English, the China storefront product page mirrors your US AirPlay marketing gaps:

  • English app name or subtitle — Search results and the product header show Latin script while competitors read native
  • Untranslated keyword field — wasted 100-character cap; China Search indexes Simplified Chinese characters, not English "AirPlay" or "Cast to TV" alone
  • English description — long body text that never mentions 隔空播放, 投屏到电视, or how playback moves to Apple TV and HomePod
  • AirPlay screenshot captions still in English — overlay lines like "AirPlay", "Cast to TV", "Watch on the big screen", "Play on HomePod", "Stream to your TV", or "Works with AirPlay" on gallery frames targeting China buyers
  • Spatial Audio or Background Audio overclaimed — description promises immersive spatial sound or phone-only background play when your app only markets wireless casting — or claims CarPlay when gallery art shows living-room TV playback
  • App Preview voiceover or burned-in English — Connect preview text fields can be zh-Hans even when video assets still carry English; redesigning burned-in video text is outside AppLocale scope

Better zh-Hans listing copy reduces product-page bounce for users who already search in Chinese — it does not auto-translate route picker labels after install.

Common mistakes on AirPlay zh-Hans listings

  • Leaving "AirPlay" untranslated — Apple markets 隔空播放 in zh-Hans regions; English-only overlay lines on otherwise Chinese copy looks unfinished
  • Machine-translated "Cast to TV" as literal 投到电视 — awkward on marketing frames; align with buyer-facing terms like 投屏到 Apple TV or 大屏观看 depending on your UX
  • Claiming Spatial Audio when you only ship AirPlay casting — metadata must match delivery; do not promise head-tracked immersive sound unless your build and gallery show it
  • Claiming Background Audio for cast-only apps — phone lock-screen Now Playing is a different buyer story from wireless TV playback
  • Conflating AirPlay with Picture in Picture — PiP is floating video on the same device; AirPlay is routing to external receivers
  • Caption lines that describe CarPlay-only playback — screenshot shows dash now-playing UI but description never explains living-room TV casting honestly; see CarPlay listing guide when the gallery leads with in-car UI
  • Claiming SharePlay for solo AirPlay casting — shared FaceTime sessions are not the same as picking Apple TV from a route picker
  • Assuming AVRoutePickerView work localizes the store page — engineering and App Store metadata are independent workstreams

FAQ

Does localizing my listing implement AirPlay routing in the app?

No. AppLocale rewrites App Store Connect metadata — name, subtitle, keywords, description, and screenshot caption lines on your zh-Hans product page. AVRoutePickerView, MPVolumeView, AVPlayer route-sharing, AirPlay receiver discovery, and hotel-TV pairing flows are engineering tasks outside AppLocale scope.

How is AirPlay listing copy different from Spatial Audio, Background Audio, Picture in Picture, CarPlay, or SharePlay?

AirPlay is wireless casting to Apple TV, HomePod, AirPlay speakers, or compatible TVs. Spatial Audio is immersive head-tracked sound on headphones. Background Audio is keep listening when you leave the app on the phone. Picture in Picture is floating video on the same device. CarPlay is in-dash navigation and audio UI. SharePlay is FaceTime shared watching or listening sessions. AirPlay listing copy covers cast to TV, play on HomePod, and big-screen or speaker routing on the product page — not those other features unless your gallery actually shows them. AirPlay ≠ Spatial Audio ≠ Background Audio ≠ Picture in Picture ≠ CarPlay ≠ SharePlay.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans AirPlay listing fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters on the zh-Hans row. The keyword field allows up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but should stay concise — especially subtitle and overlay lines that must fit on-device mockups showing AirPlay picker UI, Apple TV living-room art, or HomePod speaker marketing frames.

Should I claim Spatial Audio or Background Audio if my app only markets AirPlay casting?

No. Listing copy should describe the wireless casting experience your app actually ships — without promising Spatial Audio, phone-only Background Audio, same-device Picture in Picture, in-car CarPlay, or SharePlay FaceTime sessions your binary and gallery do not show. AppLocale rewrites from your English source claims; we do not invent surfaces your build does not support.
